judged_text: The webhook's credential upsert is a findFirst-then-update/create sequence with no unique constraint on (userId, appId), no transaction, and no idempotency guard. Two overlapping deliveries of the same webhook (senders commonly retry while a slow first request is still in flight) both see no credential and both create one, leaving duplicate rows for the same user and app; findFirst then returns an arbitrary row, so the stale duplicate intermittently serves expired keys — users see intermittent auth failures with no error surfaced anywhere.

adjudication.rationale: In the new webhook handler `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the credential write is implemented as a non-atomic `findFirst` followed by `update` or `create` (see `prisma.credential.findFirst(...)` then `prisma.credential.create(...)`). There is no transaction, no Prisma `upsert`, and no idempotency key/guard, so concurrent/retried webhook deliveries can race: both requests can observe “no credential” and attempt `create`, which can either (a) create duplicates if the DB schema does not enforce uniqueness, or (b) throw on a unique constraint if it does—either way causing broken behavior under common retry patterns.
